title: Build a Learning Culture
editorial_note: Opening revised to lead with the lesson itself. Remaining dialogue is an automated editorial draft; review spoken wording and meaning before final publication.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Build a Learning Culture.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A learning culture is not a slogan about curiosity. It is a system in which assumptions can be tested, unfavourable evidence can travel, decisions can change, and learning remains discoverable.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Culture is incentives plus operating infrastructure
turns.text: What changes when we look at culture is incentives plus operating infrastructure?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Its infrastructure includes:

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: shared definitions for outcomes, metrics, populations, and events; linked repositories for research, experiments, decisions, and source evidence; templates that record hypotheses, predictions, guardrails, and limitations before results; review rituals for proposals, trust checks, results, and post-launch outcomes; clear decision owners and escalation rights; data-quality stewardship and reproducible analysis; accessible ways for frontline and customer evidence to reach teams; time and funding for discovery, replication, maintenance, and follow-up.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Infrastructure without incentives becomes paperwork. If careers reward only launches and positive lifts, teams choose trivial tests, hide uncertainty, reinterpret null results, and avoid retiring weak ideas. Leaders must distinguish an honest failed prediction from negligent process.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at make a decision record useful?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A durable record contains context, decision, alternatives, assumptions, evidence, metric definitions, affected populations, dissent, chosen action, owner, date, expected outcome, guardrails, residual uncertainty, and review trigger. Link it to underlying material and later outcomes.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Institutional memory should support retrieval by problem, mechanism, population, metric, and decision—not only project name. Preserve negative and null results. Record why evidence was considered sufficient at the time so changed conditions can reopen the decision intelligently.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Use lightweight formats for low-risk choices and stronger governance for consequential changes. The purpose is not documentation volume; it is preventing reasoning loss.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at measure learning without gaming it?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Experiment count is an activity metric. More tests can mean trivial questions or fragmented experiences.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Better indicators include time from consequential question to decision, share of high-risk assumptions tested before commitment, recurrence of known defects, proportion of decisions with follow-up outcomes, use of prior evidence, data-quality failure detection, and time to contain harm.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Combine numbers with review of decision quality. “Ideas killed” can become as gameable as “experiments won.” The objective is better adaptation, not maximal rejection.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: repeated onboarding research?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Three teams separately learn that business customers need colleague approval before setup. Each stores findings under its feature name, so the organisation keeps designing single-user onboarding. A repository organised by job, actor, and dependency reveals the repeated structural insight and changes product strategy. Storage becomes learning only when it changes decisions.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at where this can go wrong?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Outcome theatre: delivery or favourable movement substitutes for learning. Institutional amnesia: evidence and definitions cannot be found or trusted. Punished uncertainty: teams hide risk and avoid consequential questions. Repository graveyard: documents accumulate without decision links or stewardship. Experiment factory: test volume replaces strategic relevance.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Learning without action: insight has no owner, authority, or review point. Hero analytics: critical knowledge depends on one person rather than shared systems.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Make learning change decisions and memory
turns.text: What changes when we look at make learning change decisions and memory?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The research and experiment repository records hypothesis, context, method, evidence, counterevidence, decision, and later outcome. Null and negative results remain findable. Teams revisit assumptions when service conditions change rather than treating prior findings as timeless facts. Review forums reward clear model updates, not only successful launches.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Senior practitioners model epistemic humility in public. They state what would change their mind, invite dissent before commitment, protect independent quality checks, and publish reversals without blame.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: They also prevent “learning” from becoming endless delay: decisions have owners and deadlines, evidence thresholds match consequence, and residual uncertainty is consciously accepted.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Learning must cross boundaries. A patient-safety signal cannot remain in research while product optimises conversion; a support pattern cannot remain in operations while design debates copy. Governance determines which evidence can stop work and who is accountable for response.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Make correction safer than defending the roadmap
turns.text: What changes when we look at make correction safer than defending the roadmap?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Leaders protect time for discovery, require guardrails, and avoid punishing teams for disproving a valued idea. Dashboards remain linked to customer evidence; experiment results include failures and nulls; post-launch review can reverse a feature. Psychological safety is necessary but not sufficient—authority and funding must allow action on the learning.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: <! -- Editorial: manual revision; curated product example --

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Illustrative scenario: an enterprise support portal. Teams repeatedly ship fixes for the most visible complaint without checking whether the underlying issue changed. A learning culture makes the decision, prediction, evidence, and follow-up visible. When a change fails, the team revises its model and shares the result instead of quietly moving the metric or blaming users.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Ask where your team would find a failed study from eighteen months ago. Could you recover the metric definition, population, alternative considered, and later outcome? Every missing link is institutional learning debt.
